lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay, I think that's most of us. Can everyone hear me alright?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Loud and clear. Morning, everyone.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yep, you're good.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I can hear you, I just can't find my headphones, so if there's a dog barking in the background, that's Biscuit, and I apologize in advance.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Biscuit is welcome. Biscuit has more tenure than half of this company.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Biscuit has better retention numbers than we do, too.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Ouch. Okay, we'll get to that. Are we waiting on anyone? I see Arjun, Hannah, Sofia. Where's, oh there's Sofia.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Sorry, sorry, I was in the wrong link. The calendar invite had two links on it for some reason.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's on me, I edited it last night and it duplicated the conference thing. Okay. So, is Priya recording this?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I am. It's recording now, and the notes will go out automatically afterwards, so nobody needs to take minutes. Just talk.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Which is the dream, honestly. Using our own tools, sort of.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Well, not our tool, but a tool. Okay, let's get going, because we have a lot to cover and I want to actually leave this meeting with decisions, not just vibes.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: So the goal of this session. It's the Q4 roadmap planning. We have about an hour.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I want us to walk out with three things.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: One, an agreed list of what we're doing in Q4, and just as important, what we are not doing.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Two, a named owner and a date for every big item.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And three, some kind of alignment on the AI Insights question, because I know that's been, let's say, a spirited topic on Slack.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Spirited is a very diplomatic word.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'd say it's been, yeah, it's been lively.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Right. So here's how I want to run it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: We'll start with a quick Q3 retro, just the numbers, no finger pointing.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Then Siobhan's going to walk us through what customers are actually telling us.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Then we'll do the AI Insights debate properly, then platform and reliability with Arjun and Priya, then pricing and packaging with Sofia, then hiring.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And then we'll vote and assign owners.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Are we actually voting? Like, a real vote?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: A real vote. Everyone gets three votes. It's not binding, I reserve the right to overrule everybody, but I want to see where the room is.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Benevolent dictatorship. Love it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's the startup way. Okay, and one more framing thing before we dive in.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: The company goal for Q4 is to get from where we ended Q3, which is about 3.58 million in ARR, to 4.2 million by December 31st.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's the number I've told the board. And the second goal is net revenue retention back above 110 percent.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Everything we pick today should ladder up to one of those two.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And can I add one, just so we're honest about it?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I think there's an implicit third goal, which is we need a story for the market.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Every competitor has an AI thing now, and we don't.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I'll take that as an input, not a goal, and we'll argue about it in section four.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: That's fair. I'll hold my fire.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: For about ten minutes.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: For about ten minutes, yes.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Q3 retro. Priya, do you want to go first on the engineering side, or James on revenue?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I'll go first, because mine's shorter and the news is mostly good.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Go for it.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: So, Q3 in one line. We closed 41 new logos, which is our best quarter ever, up from 29 in Q2.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: New ARR booked was about 612 thousand. The bad part is that most of that is Starter and low-end Growth.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Average deal size actually dropped, from about 18 thousand to just under 15.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And why did it drop? Is that the self-serve funnel doing more of the work, or are we discounting?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Bit of both. Self-serve is doing more, which is good.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: But honestly, we did discount more than I'd like on Growth deals at the end of the quarter.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: The last two weeks of September were, uh, a little bit of a bazaar.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I noticed. I got three accounts in onboarding with 30 percent off and no annual commitment.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Yeah, those were my calls, I own that. The logic was, get them in, prove the value, expand them later.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Which only works if they stick around. Okay, keep going.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Enterprise. We closed two Enterprise deals, Harbor Freight Systems and Lumen Health, together about 190 thousand.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Pipeline for Q4 Enterprise is 1.9 million, weighted it's probably around 560.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Win rate was 23 percent overall, and that's down from 27.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And where are we losing?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I'll get to that, it's in Siobhan's section too, but the short version is we lost six deals in Q3 where the stated reason was some version of, the other guys have AI.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Six.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Six that I'm confident about. Might be more where they just didn't tell us.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: See, this is what I've been saying.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Tom.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'm holding my fire. I'm just noting it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Noted. Priya?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Okay. So engineering Q3. The honest summary is we shipped a lot, but we shipped late, and reliability was not good enough.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: What shipped. Alerts version two went out in July, and adoption is great, about 44 percent of active workspaces have at least one alert configured now.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The Snowflake connector went GA in August. And we did the new onboarding flow, which Sofia can speak to, but I think it moved trial activation a bit.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: It did. Activation, meaning a workspace sends events and builds a first dashboard within seven days, went from 31 to 38 percent.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's a big jump.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: It is. Trial to paid didn't move as much though. We're at 11.2 percent, target was 14.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: And then what didn't ship. SSO and SCIM slipped. We said August, it's still not done.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The dashboard builder rework slipped about five weeks, and we ended up descoping half of it.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: The SSO one hurts, just so everyone knows. That's come up in every single Enterprise security review.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I know. I know. I'll talk about why when we get to platform, but the short version is that the same three people who own auth also got pulled into every incident.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Which brings us to incidents.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Right. We had three sev ones in Q3.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The worst was August 14th, the ingestion lag, where events were delayed up to six hours for about a third of customers.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Uptime for the quarter was 99.82 percent, and our contractual SLA for Enterprise is 99.9.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: So we breached.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: We breached for the quarter, yes. Technically we owe service credits to the two Enterprise customers who asked, and we've paid them.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: It was about 4 thousand dollars total. The money isn't the problem, the trust is.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: And just to add some color on that. The August 14th thing wasn't a one-off.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: It's the same root cause as the June incident.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: The ingestion workers are sharing a single Postgres queue table, and when one big customer backfills, everybody else waits.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: We've known about that for a while though, right?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: We've known since March. It's been on the list. It keeps losing to features.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Fair.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay, and I want to be clear, that's on me as much as anyone, because I've been the one pushing features.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Let's keep going. Siobhan, retention numbers?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Sure. So net revenue retention for Q3 came in at 104 percent. It was 111 in Q2.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Gross logo churn on Starter is running about 2.9 percent a month, which is high but kind of expected for that tier.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Growth tier churn is 1.4 percent a month, and that's the one that worries me, because those are real companies paying us six grand a year.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Is that mostly the discounted ones?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Some of them, but no, not mostly. Most of the Growth churn is accounts that have been with us for more than a year.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: They grew, their event volume grew, dashboards got slow, and they left for something that felt faster or smarter.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: So it's performance.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: It's performance and it's the, what do I do with this data problem. I'll get into it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Perfect segue. Anything else on the retro before we move on? Hannah, anything from the ML side for Q3?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Um, just that the anomaly detection model for alerts is live on about 900 workspaces. Nothing else really.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's great, and that's actually relevant for later. Okay. Siobhan, you're up.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Okay. So for this, my team went through every support ticket from Q3, that's 212 tickets that weren't just password resets, plus the notes from 38 customer interviews, plus the churn exit surveys.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: And we tagged all of it. I'll share the doc after, but I want to give you the top four themes, roughly in order.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Great, go.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Theme one, and it's the biggest by a lot.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Customers can see that a number moved, but they can't figure out why.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: That came up in 71 tickets and in 24 of the 38 interviews.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: The quote I keep coming back to is from the head of growth at Parcelly.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: She said, and I'm reading it, your dashboards are great at telling me something is on fire, and useless at telling me where the fire is.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: That's a great quote. Can we put that on the wall?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: You can put it on the wall. It's a bit painful for a product called Pulse, though.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: That's exactly the problem AI Insights solves.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Tom.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Sorry. Holding. Still holding.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I mean, he's not wrong, but let me get through them. Theme two is speed.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Dashboards on large workspaces are slow. We have eleven accounts where the median dashboard load is over eight seconds.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Globex is one of them, and I'll come back to Globex, because it's a big deal.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Is that eleven accounts from the ticket tags or from the telemetry?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Telemetry. Arjun's team gave me the numbers.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Yeah, that's from the query logs. p95 across all workspaces is about 4.1 seconds, which is not great, but for the top fifty workspaces by event volume, p95 is 8.4 seconds.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: And a few of them time out entirely on thirty-day ranges.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I've seen demos go sideways because of that.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: We use the demo workspace, which is small, and then they load their own data in the trial and it crawls.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Theme three is security and admin. SSO, SCIM, audit logs, role-based permissions.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: It's lower volume, only 19 tickets, but it's almost all from our biggest accounts, and it's blocking expansions.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: And new deals. I have two Enterprise deals in the pipe right now, Meridian Freight and Castellan, where the security questionnaire literally has SSO as a hard requirement.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: What's the combined value of those two?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: About 240 thousand a year combined.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: And then theme four is pricing confusion, specifically the event overages.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: People don't understand what an event is, they don't understand why their bill went up, and they find out after the fact.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: We had 27 tickets that were basically, why is my invoice higher than I expected.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: And three of the Growth churns in Q3 explicitly mentioned a surprise overage bill.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: That one's mine, and I have a proposal for it later.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Great. So, those are the four. Now, Globex. Globex renews on January 31st.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: They're at 186 thousand a year, they're our second biggest customer.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I had their QBR last week with Greg Holloway and Maya Lindqvist, and I'll be blunt, they are at risk.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: How at risk?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I'd put it at maybe fifty-fifty right now.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Greg said, pretty directly, that his team is evaluating Amplitude, and that the two things that would keep them are dashboard performance and SSO.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: He also said, and this is interesting, that if we had something that could explain metric changes automatically, they'd pay more for it, not less.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Did he say that? He said they'd pay more?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: He said, and again I'm paraphrasing a little, if you could tell my exec team why the numbers moved before they ask me, I would find budget for that.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay, I need everyone to remember that sentence.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I also need everyone to remember the first half, which is fix the performance and ship SSO.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Both halves are true. That's kind of my whole point. The AI stuff is a reason to expand.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Performance and SSO are the reason they stay at all.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's a really useful framing. Hannah, you've been quiet. Does the explain-the-change thing match what you've seen?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Yeah. Yes, it does.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. James, the six lost deals?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Right. So, six deals, about 310 thousand in total ACV.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Four went to Amplitude, one went to Mixpanel, one went to, I think, building it in-house on dbt and Hex.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: In five of the six, the AI features came up in the final stage.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Not necessarily because they'd use them, honestly. In a couple of cases I think it was more that the buyer needed something to show their boss.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: But that still matters. That's the story for the market point.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: It does matter. I'm not arguing it doesn't.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I'm just saying, in two of those deals, if we'd had SSO we might have won anyway, because the AI thing was a tiebreaker, not the main reason.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Can I add one more thing from the interviews? It's small but I think it's important.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: When we asked people what they'd want from AI, nobody said a chatbot. Not one person.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: What they said was, tell me what changed, tell me why, and tell me who to ask about it.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: It's very specific. It's basically root cause analysis.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Which is exactly the scope of the Explain This Change prototype.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. I think that's a natural place to move into the AI Insights discussion.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Siobhan, thank you, that was really clear. Please send the doc around.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Will do. I'll send it right after this.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: So. AI Insights. Tom, you've been holding your fire for twenty minutes. The floor is yours.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And then Priya, I want you to respond, and then everybody else.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Thank you. Okay. I'll try to be concise.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That'll be a first.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Wow. Okay. Fair. So here's the pitch. We build AI Insights as the headline feature for Q4.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: The core of it is Explain This Change.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: When a metric on a dashboard moves more than some threshold, you click on it, and we tell you which segments drove the change, which events, which properties, and we write a plain-English explanation.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Hannah's prototype already does a version of this.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Phase two, which is not Q4, would be proactive.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: We'd push the explanation into Slack or email before anyone asks, which is literally what Greg at Globex said he'd pay for.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And my ask is that we ship a beta to customers by mid November, and that we staff it with, call it, four engineers plus Hannah, for the whole quarter.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Because if we don't have something real by the time budgets get set in January, I think we lose more deals like the six James just described.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Thank you. Priya?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: So, first, I'm not against AI Insights. I want to say that clearly, because I think Slack made it sound like I am.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I think it's the right direction. I think the prototype is really promising.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: My problem is sequencing and capacity. We have eleven engineers.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: If four of them go to AI Insights for the whole quarter, plus the three on auth for SSO, that leaves four people for everything else, including the ingestion rework that Arjun described, which is the root cause of two sev ones.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: And here's the thing that I think gets missed. Explain This Change runs queries. Lots of queries.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: It's basically going to slice every metric by every dimension to find the driver.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: If our query layer can't load a dashboard in under eight seconds for Globex, it's definitely not going to run a root cause analysis across fifty segments in any reasonable time.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: But that's a solvable problem, you can precompute--

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You can precompute if you have a working aggregation layer, which we don't yet. That's the ingestion and query work.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Yeah, I want to back that up with numbers, if that's okay.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: So Hannah and I actually ran the prototype against the Globex dataset last week, just to see.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: On their thirty-day event table, one Explain This Change run took about 94 seconds and scanned around 1.3 billion rows.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: The warehouse cost for that one run was about 60 cents.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Plus the LLM call on top, which is small, maybe four cents.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Ninety-four seconds.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Ninety-four seconds. And if a customer clicks it on every chart on a dashboard, you do the math.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Sixty cents a click. Globex would click that a thousand times a month.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: And that's one customer.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay, but the competitors are eating that cost. Amplitude isn't charging sixty cents a click.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Do we actually know that? What their thing costs them?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: No. But their customers don't pay per click, I know that much.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: They also have, what, eight hundred engineers? We have eleven.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Fair. Fair.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Can I say something about the Amplitude thing specifically? Because Greg showed it to me on the QBR.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: He pulled it up on screen share. It's a chat box.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: You ask it a question and it builds you a chart.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: And he said, and this is a direct quote, it's a nice party trick, but I don't need a new chart, I need someone to tell me why the old chart went down.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Huh.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: So I don't think we're behind on the thing customers actually want. I think we're behind on the demo.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Which, to be fair, is what wins deals in the final round.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Sure, but it's not what keeps them for three years.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I have to win them before you can keep them.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: And I have to keep them or your new logos just refill a leaky bucket.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay, okay. You're both right, and that's exactly why this is hard.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: For what it's worth, the chat-box thing is actually much cheaper to build.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: It's text-to-SQL on top of our query layer. The expensive part is the root cause search.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: So you're saying the thing customers want is the expensive one.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: It's always the expensive one.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That's basically the first law of product management.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I thought the first law was, the customer is always right.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: The first law is, the customer is always right about the problem and always wrong about the solution.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay, I'm stealing that.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Hannah, can the prototype be made cheaper without the rollups? Like, sample the data?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: A bit. We could sample ten percent of events for the search, and then confirm the top candidates on the full data.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: That might get it to, um, maybe fifteen or twenty seconds on Globex.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: But the accuracy drops a little.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: I don't know yet. I'd have to test it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. That's a useful fallback to keep in our back pocket.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: And to be clear, I think that's a good backup plan, but it's not the main plan.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The main plan is the rollups.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Understood.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay, but, and I'm genuinely asking, how much of that goes away with the aggregation work?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Like, if Arjun's rework lands, what does that run look like?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Honestly, rough estimate, with pre-aggregated hourly rollups by the top twenty dimensions, it's probably under five seconds and a couple of cents.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: But that's the rollup work, and that's six to eight weeks.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: So the rollups make AI Insights possible.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: The rollups make AI Insights possible, and they make dashboards fast, and they make the ingestion lag problem mostly go away. It's the same project.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's interesting. So they're not actually in competition. They're a dependency.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That's exactly my point. It's not AI Insights versus reliability. It's reliability, and then AI Insights on top of it.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I hear that. My worry is timing. If the rollups take eight weeks, and they start in October, that's end of November.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Then AI Insights on top of that is January at the earliest. And we've missed the budget cycle.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: For what it's worth, the budget cycle point is real.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Most of my Enterprise buyers lock their tooling budgets in December.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Right, but they don't lock them based on a beta.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: They lock them based on a demo and a roadmap commitment. You can sell a credible roadmap.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You can't sell an outage.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Well, I've sold a few roadmaps in my time, that's true.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Let's not put that in the recording.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: It's already in the recording.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Great. Okay. Hannah, I'm going to put you on the spot, because this is your prototype.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: How good is it actually, right now?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Um. So. On our internal eval set, which is about 150 historical metric changes where we know the actual cause, the prototype identifies the right driver in the top three about 62 percent of the time.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Which is pretty good for a prototype.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: It's okay. It's not good enough to put in front of Globex.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: If it's wrong a third of the time, people stop trusting it, and then they stop trusting the dashboards too.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: I think we'd need to be at 75, maybe 80, before a wide beta.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: How long to get from 62 to 75?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Maybe six weeks, if I get one more engineer and the rollups.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Without the rollups it's hard to iterate, every eval run takes hours.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. That's really helpful, thank you.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Can I propose something? Because I think there's a middle path here.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Please, yes.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: What if we do a scoped beta. Not a launch, a design-partner beta.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Ten customers, Growth and Enterprise only, behind a feature flag.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: We pick customers whose data is small enough that it runs fine today, or we precompute for just them.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: It gives James something real to demo and something to put in the roadmap deck, and it gives Hannah real feedback to improve the model.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: But we don't staff it with four engineers. We staff it with Hannah plus one.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Ten is small.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Ten is small on purpose. We learn, and we don't put our reputation on the line with a 62 percent model.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: And I can find ten. I already have a list of maybe fifteen accounts who've asked for exactly this.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Parcelly would be first in line.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And Globex?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Globex, I'm not sure. Their data is huge. If it takes ninety seconds for them, that's worse than nothing.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: We could precompute rollups for Globex specifically, as a pilot of the rollup design.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: That's actually a nice forcing function for my team. It de-risks the general rollout.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I like that. That's a real test on the hardest dataset.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay. I'll be honest, this isn't what I wanted. I wanted a big launch.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: But I think I can live with the design-partner version, if, and this is my condition, we commit to a date.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: A real date. Not, when the rollups are done.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: What date would you want?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Beta live with the first design partners by November 20th.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: November 20th with Hannah plus one engineer, and it depends on the Globex rollup pilot being done by, what, Arjun?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: If we start Monday, I think the Globex rollups could be ready by November 6th. The general rollout is later.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Then November 20th is aggressive but doable. I'll commit to it if the one engineer is Marcus, because he knows the query layer.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Marcus is great. Done.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Wait, let's not say done yet, Marcus isn't here to be volunteered.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: He volunteered on Tuesday. His cost doc is one of the pre-reads for today, actually, and he's been asking to work on this for a month.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: It's part of his growth plan.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay, great. Then let me say it back so it's crisp, because this is the first real decision of the meeting.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Decision. AI Insights ships in Q4 as a design-partner beta of Explain This Change only.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Ten design partners, Growth and Enterprise tier, behind a feature flag. Staffed by Hannah plus Marcus.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Target: live with the first partners by November 20th.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: We do not do a public launch or general availability in Q4.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And the proactive, push-to-Slack piece is explicitly out of scope for this quarter.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Agreed. Reluctantly, but agreed.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Agreed.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Can I still talk about it in sales conversations? Like, as a roadmap item?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Yes, as roadmap. Beta for design partners, GA in the first half of next year.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Don't promise dates to customers beyond that.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Got it. First half of next year. I can work with that.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: And, sorry, one thing. We need a quality bar before we turn it on for anyone.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: I'd like it to be 75 percent top-three accuracy on the eval set.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Good. Let's make that part of the decision.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: No partner sees it until the eval is at 75 percent. Hannah owns that bar.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Okay. Thank you.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And what happens if we're at 70 on November 20th?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Then we're at 70, and we wait.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Fair enough. I'd rather be late than wrong. I think.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: That's the first time I've heard you say that.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Don't get used to it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Let's move to platform and reliability, because I think a lot of this depends on that. Arjun, Priya, who's driving?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Arjun, go ahead, it's your plan. I'll jump in on staffing.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Sure. So I'll try to keep this tight.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: There are three problems, and they all have the same shape.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Ingestion lag, slow dashboards, and our on-call load.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: And the root cause is, basically, we built the platform for customers sending ten million events a month, and our top fifty customers now send between 200 million and two billion.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: So the plan has three parts. Part one, ingestion.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: We move off the shared Postgres queue table onto partitioned Kafka topics, partitioned by workspace.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: That means one customer's backfill can't block everyone else.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: We've already got Kafka running for the Snowflake connector, so it's not a new technology for us.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Part two, the rollups we talked about. Hourly pre-aggregations for the most common metric and dimension combinations.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Dashboards read from rollups first, and only hit raw events when they need to.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: That's what gets p95 dashboard load from 8.4 seconds down to, my target is 2.5 seconds for the top fifty workspaces.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Part three is operational. We fix alerting so the on-call person isn't getting paged for things that don't matter.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Last month the on-call rotation got 143 pages. About 70 percent of those were noise.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Kevin has a plan for that.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: A hundred and forty-three pages in a month.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: In a month. Kevin had a week where he got paged at 3 AM four nights in a row.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: And that's why I'm worried about burnout. Two people on the platform team have mentioned it in one-on-ones.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I don't want to lose people over this.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Understood. That's not acceptable. What's the timeline on all three parts?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Ingestion migration, I'd say the design doc by October 9th, and cutover done by October 30th.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Rollups, general availability for all workspaces by the end of November, with the Globex pilot by November 6th like I said.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: And the alerting cleanup, Kevin thinks two weeks, so by October 17th.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And how many people is that?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: The whole platform team, so four, plus I'd want one more from product engineering for the first three weeks.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Basically I'm asking for a code yellow.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Sorry, what's a code yellow? Is that a Google thing?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: It's a Google thing, yeah. It means reliability is the top priority for a fixed period.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: People can get pulled from feature work, and nothing ships that increases risk unless it's critical.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Okay, so a feature freeze.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Not a full freeze. More like, a soft freeze, for a defined window.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'd propose the first three weeks of October. So October 6th through October 24th. Three full weeks.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Three weeks of soft freeze. Hmm.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Tom, I can see your face.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'm not saying no. I'm doing math. What's frozen, exactly? Because the sharing work is basically done.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Sharing is fine, Nina's rolling it out this week. That's already in flight, it's low risk.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay. And the pricing page changes?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Those are mostly front end and billing config. They land in November anyway.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Then they're fine too. What's frozen is anything that touches ingestion, the query layer, or auth, unless it's part of the reliability work or SSO.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And the dashboard builder v2?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Frozen. Honestly, I think it should move to Q1 anyway, but let's get to that in the vote.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: We'll fight about that in the vote.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: We will.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: What about customer-specific requests? Like if Meridian needs some small thing to close.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Come to me. If it's small and it closes a deal, we'll find a way.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Just don't promise it on the call first.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: That's fair. I'll try.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Try harder than last quarter.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Ha. Okay. Noted.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Arjun, what's the risk on the Kafka migration itself? I don't want the cure to cause another sev one.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Good question. The risk is real. The plan is to dual-write for a week.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Old queue and new topics in parallel, and we compare counts.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: We only cut over when the counts match for seven straight days.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And rollback?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Rollback is flipping a flag back to the old queue. We'll keep it warm until end of November.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. I like that.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: And Kevin's adding a canary for the consumer deploys. That was the main action item from last week's incident review.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Good. Siobhan, from your side, what would a code yellow mean for customers? Do we tell them?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I'd tell the big ones. Not with the phrase code yellow, obviously.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: No. Nobody wants to hear their vendor is in code anything.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Right. I'd say something like, we're investing the next month in performance and reliability, here's what you'll see.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: For Globex specifically, I think that message could actually help the renewal.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: I can give you a one-pager with the before and after numbers. Once we have them.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: That would be perfect. Honestly, the funnel improvement Marcus did already helped. Greg mentioned it on the call.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Two point eight seconds to nine hundred milliseconds on their funnels. That was one engineer, one week.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: See, that's the kind of thing we should shout about.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I did shout about it. Greg was, and I quote, mildly impressed.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: From Greg, that's a standing ovation.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: That's basically a parade.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Then let's capture it. Decision two. We run a reliability code yellow from October 6th to October 24th.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Platform team full time, plus one product engineer.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Feature work that touches ingestion, query, or auth is frozen in that window unless Priya approves it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And the targets are, Arjun, say them again?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: p95 dashboard load under 2.5 seconds for the top fifty workspaces. Ingestion lag under five minutes at p99.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: And pages to on-call down by at least 60 percent.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And uptime?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: 99.9 or better for Q4. That's the SLA, so that's the floor.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'd also like us to add a public status page.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: We don't have one, and customers find out about incidents from Twitter.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Do we really not have a status page?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: We have an internal one. The external one has been on the list since, I want to say, February.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Let's do it. Who owns that?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Kevin can own it. It's maybe two days of work with an off-the-shelf tool.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Great, Kevin by the end of the code yellow then. Priya, you'll tell him he volunteered?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'll break it to him gently.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Now SSO and SCIM. Priya, where are we really?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Really? SAML SSO is about 80 percent done. It works with Okta in staging.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Azure AD has an issue with group claims. SCIM is maybe 40 percent. Audit logs haven't started.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: What's the date? That's the only thing I need. A date I can put in a security questionnaire.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'll give you a date, but I want to give you one I'll actually hit this time.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: SAML SSO with Okta and Azure AD, generally available on November 2nd. SCIM provisioning on November 16th.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Audit logs slip to Q1.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Can I say November for both?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You can say SSO in early November and SCIM by mid November.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Please don't round it to November 1st, I'll get paged about it.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Ha. Okay. November 2nd and mid November.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: That works for Globex too. Their renewal is January 31st, so that gives them two months of having it before they decide.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And the three auth engineers are protected from incidents during that window?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That's the point of the code yellow. Platform takes the incidents. Auth ships.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Decision three, then. SSO GA November 2nd, SCIM November 16th, audit logs to Q1.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Priya owns it, weekly status in the eng update.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yep. I'll post it every Friday.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Can I say one thing before we leave platform?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Quickly.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I just want to acknowledge, I think Priya and Arjun were right about sequencing.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I came in wanting AI Insights to be the whole quarter, and I think the rollups argument is correct.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'd rather say that out loud than just quietly lose the argument.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Thank you. That's, honestly, that's really nice to hear.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Appreciated, Tom.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's the most grown-up thing anyone has said in a roadmap meeting at this company.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Don't worry, I'll ruin it during pricing.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I have no doubt. Sofia, pricing. You're up.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Okay. I'll share my screen. Can everyone see the spreadsheet?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I see it. I see a lot of yellow cells.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: The yellow cells are the ones I'm unsure about. So, ignore those for now.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Okay, the problem, very briefly. Siobhan mentioned it. Growth is $499 a month and includes 5 million events.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Above that, we charge overages at $40 per extra million, billed in arrears.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Customers don't see it coming and they hate it.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Hate is accurate.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: And meanwhile, the median Growth customer is now at 11 million events a month.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: So the median customer is paying overages, which means the $499 price is basically fiction.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: What's the median Growth customer actually paying?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: About $740 a month, all in.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Huh. Okay.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: So the proposal. Growth goes to $599 a month, and includes 20 million events instead of 5.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Above 20 million, it's $25 per extra million, not $40.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: And the big change, we show the usage meter in the app and we email at 80 percent and 100 percent of the included volume. No surprises.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Wait, so for the median customer at 11 million, they'd pay less?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Yes. They'd go from $740 to $599. That's on purpose.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: That's a revenue cut.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: For some existing customers, yes, which is why I'm proposing we don't force-migrate anyone.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: But for new customers, the math is different.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Our new Growth customers start at about 3 million events and grow into overages.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Under the new pricing, they start at $599 instead of $499.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: So new-customer ACV goes up about 20 percent.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And we stop being the vendor with the surprise bill.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Exactly. I modeled it out. Net effect over twelve months is roughly plus 6 percent revenue on Growth, and I think it helps churn, which I haven't put in the model because I can't prove it.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I can basically prove it. Three churns last quarter said surprise overage. That's about 21 thousand in ARR, right there.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. What about existing customers?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Grandfather them. They keep their current plan for twelve months.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: They can opt in to the new plan any time, and for most of them it's cheaper, so a lot of them will.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: And that's the part I'm worried about. If it's cheaper and they opt in, that's a downgrade on my number.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: For about 40 percent of existing Growth accounts it's cheaper, yes.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: For the rest, it's more expensive, so they won't switch.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: So I lose on 40 percent and gain on zero percent of the existing base.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: In the short term. Yeah.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: That's a hard sell to my team. They get paid on net ARR.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Hmm. How much are we talking about?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: If every single one of those 40 percent switched on day one, which they won't, it's about 54 thousand in ARR.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Realistically, maybe half that over the year.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Twenty-seven thousand against the churn risk and new-customer uplift. James, I hear you, but I think that's worth it.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I don't disagree with the strategy. I'm worried about the comp plan.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: If a rep's customer switches plans and their number goes down, I'll have a mutiny.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Then we fix the comp plan so reps aren't penalized for a customer moving to the new plan.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's a comp problem, not a pricing problem.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Okay. If we fix comp, I'm in. I want that in writing though.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: You'll have it in writing. I'll do it with finance.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: And just so everyone knows, the pricing page itself is mostly designed.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Tom, Leah, James and I went through it last week.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: The $25 overage and the usage calculator came out of that session.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: It's a good page. Leah did great work on it.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: The piece that session couldn't decide was the bigger question, which is the actual Growth price, and what we do with AI Insights in the packaging.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: So that's what I need from this room.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Let's take the price first. Anyone against $599 with 20 million included?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Not against. Just a question. Does 20 million events cost us more to serve than 5 million?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Because that's four times the included volume.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: It does, a little. I checked with finance.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Our infra cost per million events is about $3.10 today, and after the rollups, you said it'd drop?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: It should drop. Maybe to around $2. Storage is the big piece, and rollups let us tier the raw data to cold storage sooner.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Then the margins are fine either way. Gross margin on Growth stays above 78 percent.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Okay. No objection then.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Siobhan?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Strong yes. With the grandfathering. And the 80 percent email is the thing I care most about, honestly.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Tom?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Yes. And on AI Insights packaging, my proposal is we don't price it at all in Q4.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: It's a beta, it's for design partners, it's free.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: We decide packaging in Q1 when we know what it costs to run.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I'd love to be able to say it'll be included in Enterprise. That's a real lever in a deal.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'm okay saying Enterprise customers get early access.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'm not okay saying it's included forever, because we don't know the cost yet.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Sixty cents a click, remember.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Sixty cents a click today. Two cents after the rollups.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Hopefully.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Okay. Early access for Enterprise. I'll take it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Good. Then decision four. New Growth pricing, $599 a month with 20 million events included and $25 per additional million, goes live for new customers on November 3rd.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Existing customers are grandfathered for twelve months with an opt-in.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Usage meter and 80 and 100 percent alerts ship with it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And James and I fix the sales comp plan so reps aren't penalized for plan switches.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And AI Insights isn't priced in Q4. Enterprise gets early access, packaging decision in Q1.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Perfect. That's exactly what I needed.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: And the annual discount? That was the other thing we argued about.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: We kept it at 20 percent through Q1. That was decided in the pricing page session.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Wait, I thought we were going to 15.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: We talked about it. I pushed for keeping 20 until the end of Q1 because I have deals mid-negotiation at 20.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Hmm. I'm not thrilled, but fine. Revisit in January.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Don't let 20 percent become 30 percent at the end of the quarter, James.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: No bazaars. Understood.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay, hiring. Priya, and I'll jump in on budget.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Sure. So we have three open reqs right now.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Staff engineer on platform, an ML engineer for Hannah's team, and a customer success manager for Siobhan.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The staff engineer is the most urgent. We're mid-process with a really strong candidate. Olivia Grant.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Arjun and I interviewed her last week, and it was a strong yes from both of us.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: She built the ingestion pipeline at a logistics company doing about four billion events a day.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: She'd basically be the tech lead for the rollups phase two. She's exactly the person we need.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: What's she asking for?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: A bit above our band. About 235 base. Our band tops out at 220.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Hmm. Equity can make up some of it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I'm okay going to 228 base plus a larger grant, if she's the real deal.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: She's the real deal. I'll put the offer together.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. By when?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Offer out by next Wednesday. She has another offer expiring on the 15th, so we need to move.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Do it. Then the CSM?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: The CSM is, honestly, it's urgent for me too. I have three people covering 140 accounts.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Each Enterprise account should really have a dedicated person, and right now I'm personally covering Globex and Lumen Health.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: What would a CSM cost fully loaded?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: About 130 thousand all in.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And the ML engineer?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Um, around 210. Maybe more. It's a hard market.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. So here's my honest position. We have budget for two of the three this quarter, not all three.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Unless we beat the ARR plan.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'd argue for the ML engineer. That's the AI Insights bet.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'd argue the beta is scoped for Hannah plus Marcus now. We just decided that.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The ML engineer matters for GA, which is next year.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: But if we hire in January, they're not productive until March.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: And if Globex churns in January because nobody's managing the account, AI Insights doesn't matter.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: That's a little dramatic.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Is it? They're 186 thousand. That's more than the ML engineer and the CSM combined.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay. Okay. That's a fair point.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Hannah, you're the one who'd manage the ML engineer. What do you think?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: I think, um. Honestly, I can do the beta with Marcus.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: I'd rather have the right person in February than the wrong person in November.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Wow. Okay. Hannah just ended the argument.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I think she did. Decision five. We approve the staff engineer and the CSM now.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: The ML engineer req opens in January, and we'll revisit earlier if we're ahead of plan at the end of November.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Priya owns the Olivia offer, Siobhan owns the CSM hire.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Thank you. I'll have the job description out tomorrow.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And one more thing on capacity. Someone asked me about contractors for SSO. Priya?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'd say no. Auth is the one place I don't want someone who's leaving in three months.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The ramp-up alone would eat most of the time.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. No contractors on auth. Good.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Alright. We have about fifteen minutes left, so let's do the vote.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I'm going to read out the candidate priorities, and everyone gets three votes.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Just say your three when I call your name.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Can we pass on one and give two to something?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: No stacking. Three different things.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Worth a shot.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: The six candidates are. One, the reliability code yellow, meaning ingestion and rollups. Two, SSO and SCIM.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Three, AI Insights design-partner beta. Four, the new Growth pricing and usage meter. Five, dashboard builder v2. Six, the mobile app.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Is the mobile app still a thing?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: It's my thing. It's a small thing. Customers ask for it.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Two customers ask for it.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Two very loud customers.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: It's on the list because it was on the Q3 list. Let's see what the room says. Priya?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Reliability, SSO, and AI Insights beta.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Arjun?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Reliability, SSO, pricing.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Tom?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: AI Insights beta, reliability, and, ugh, I have to pick between pricing and dashboard builder.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: You have to pick.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Dashboard builder v2. Somebody has to stand up for it.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Noted. Sofia?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Pricing, reliability, AI Insights.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: James?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: SSO, AI Insights, pricing.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Siobhan?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Reliability, SSO, pricing.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Hannah?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Oh. Um. Reliability, AI Insights, and SSO.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And me. Reliability, SSO, and AI Insights. So let me count.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Reliability, that's Priya, Arjun, Tom, Sofia, Siobhan, Hannah, me. Seven. SSO is Priya, Arjun, James, Siobhan, Hannah, me.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Six. AI Insights is Priya, Tom, Sofia, James, Hannah, me. Six. Pricing is Arjun, Sofia, James, Siobhan. Four.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Dashboard builder is Tom. One. And mobile app is zero.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Zero. Wow. Not even me.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Not even you.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'm a realist.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. So that's very clear, and it matches the decisions we've already made, which is reassuring.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: The top four are in. Dashboard builder v2 moves to Q1. And the mobile app is cut.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Not deferred, cut. If it comes back, it comes back with real customer demand behind it.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Can we say deferred instead of cut? For morale?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: No. I think it's healthier to say cut. Deferred things never die, they just haunt the backlog.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: The backlog is basically a graveyard with a search bar.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Exactly. Decision six. Q4 priorities in order are reliability, SSO and SCIM, AI Insights beta, and Growth pricing.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Dashboard builder v2 moves to Q1. Mobile app is cut.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'll tell the two loud customers.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Thank you. And Tom, can you tell the whole company at the all-hands on Friday?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I want them to hear what we're not doing, not just what we are.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Yeah, I'll do a slide. What we're doing, what we're not doing, and why.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Owners and dates. I'm going to go person by person, and I want you to say the thing and the date out loud, so it's in the recording and nobody can claim they didn't agree to it.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: This is the part where I start sweating.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: You should. Let's start with Priya.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Okay. One, I'll send the code yellow plan to engineering, with who's pulled from what, by end of day tomorrow.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Two, SSO GA on November 2nd and SCIM on November 16th, with a status update every Friday in the eng update.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Three, the offer to Olivia goes out by next Wednesday.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Great. And the status page?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Right, sorry. Kevin owns the public status page, live by October 24th, the end of the code yellow.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'll confirm with him today.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Arjun.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: The Kafka ingestion design doc by October 9th. Dual-write starting the week after. Cutover complete by October 30th.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: And the Globex rollup pilot ready by November 6th.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Good. And the performance one-pager for Siobhan?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Oh, yes. The before and after numbers for Globex, I'll get that to Siobhan by October 27th, once we have a week of post-cutover data. Well, early data.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Early data is fine.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Hannah.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Um. So I'll get the Explain This Change eval to 75 percent top-three accuracy before any partner sees it.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: And I'll send a progress update every two weeks. The first one on October 16th.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Great. And a go or no-go call on the beta when?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: November 13th. A week before the launch date. So there's time to react.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Perfect. Tom.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: So, the AI Insights beta one-pager. What it does, what it doesn't do, and who qualifies as a design partner.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: By October 10th. And the all-hands slide on what we're doing and not doing, that's this Friday.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And talking to the two loud mobile customers?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: By the end of next week. I'll do it on a call, not an email. They deserve that.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Good. Siobhan.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Okay. First, recruit the ten AI Insights design partners, signed up by October 24th. Parcelly first.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Second, a call with Greg Holloway at Globex to walk him through the reliability plan and the SSO dates, by October 10th.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Third, the CSM job description goes out tomorrow.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And Globex as a design partner?

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I'll ask Greg on that call. If Arjun's pilot is on track, I think they'll say yes.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Maya already said she was interested in the QBR.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Great. Sofia.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: The pricing spec with final numbers and the grandfathering rules, by October 15th.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: The customer email for existing Growth accounts, drafted by October 20th, and Siobhan reviews it.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: And new pricing goes live for new customers on November 3rd.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: I'll review it within two days of getting it.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: James.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Updated Q4 forecast reflecting all of this, by October 8th.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Updated security questionnaire answers for Meridian and Castellan with the SSO dates, by October 7th.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: And sales enablement on the new pricing, a training session for the reps, by October 31st.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And the comp plan?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: That's you and me.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: That's you and me. Comp plan change so reps aren't penalized for plan switches, done with finance, by October 17th.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I own that one, James is on the hook to review it.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Happy to be on the hook for that one.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And my other one is the board update.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Q4 plan, the decisions from today, and the revised ARR bridge. By October 9th.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Can I ask one thing about the board update?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Can you frame the code yellow as an investment and not as a problem?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The team's already feeling a bit bruised about the incidents.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I don't want them to read the board deck and feel like they're the problem.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Absolutely. That's a good call. And for what it's worth, I don't think the team is the problem.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: I think the sequencing was the problem, and that was mostly my call.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Thank you. I'll pass that on.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Did I miss anyone? Hannah, Tom, Sofia, Siobhan, James, Priya, Arjun, me.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Anybody have something they think should have an owner that doesn't?

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Just one thing. The on-call noise reduction. I said Kevin thinks two weeks. Can we put that at October 17th?

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Yes. Kevin, alert cleanup, 60 percent fewer pages, by October 17th. Priya, add it to your note to him.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Got it. He's going to love me today.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Bring him a coffee.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'll bring him two.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Okay. Let me do the wrap-up. We have about three minutes, so I'll be fast.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Decisions. One, AI Insights ships in Q4 as a design-partner beta of Explain This Change.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Ten partners, Growth and Enterprise, Hannah and Marcus, live by November 20th, only if the eval hits 75 percent. No GA in Q4.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Two, reliability code yellow from October 6th to October 24th. Kafka ingestion, rollups, alert cleanup, public status page.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Three, SSO on November 2nd, SCIM on November 16th, audit logs in Q1.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Four, new Growth pricing live November 3rd, $599 with 20 million events, $25 per extra million.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Grandfathering for twelve months. Comp plan fixed.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Five, hire the staff engineer and the CSM now, ML engineer in January.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Six, priorities in order, reliability, SSO, AI Insights, pricing. Dashboard builder v2 moves to Q1. Mobile app is cut.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Anything I got wrong?

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: No. That's right. Painful, but right.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: That's right.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: That's what I heard.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Great. Then the last thing. I know this one was intense, and I know not everyone got what they wanted. Tom especially.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I'll be fine. I'll just go cry into the mobile app mockups.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: But I think this is the most honest plan we've had.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And if we hit it, we're at 4.2 million and the Globex renewal is signed, and we have an AI story we're not embarrassed by.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: And nobody gets paged at 3 AM four nights in a row.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: And nobody gets paged at 3 AM four nights in a row. That too.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Biscuit would like to add that he's very proud of everyone.

lines.speaker: siobhan
lines.text: Tell Biscuit he's in the Q4 plan now.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: He'll want equity.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Everybody wants equity. Okay. Priya, the notes will go out automatically?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yep, as soon as I stop the recording. Summary, action items, all of it.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'll share it in the leadership channel.

lines.speaker: dana
lines.text: Perfect. Thanks everyone. Great meeting. Go do the things.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Thanks, all.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Thanks. Bye.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Bye.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Bye, everyone.
